summary: Extends the Application-Layer Traffic Optimization (ALTO) protocol so that properties can describe more than just IP addresses. Entities of many kinds can carry properties, and those properties are published as maps, like the network and cost maps in the base protocol. It builds on the Endpoint Property Service from RFC 7285 and is a standards-track extension.

eli5.summary: Imagine a school directory that only listed kids by home address. This lets it list all sorts of things, like clubs and classrooms, and give each one a fact sheet, all gathered on one big chart.

subtitle: ALTO learns to attach facts to far more than IP addresses, and to publish them as whole downloadable maps.

tldr.problem: The base ALTO protocol (RFC 7285) can only attach properties to individual IP addresses, only for globally unique addresses, and only on request through a POST. Clients cannot describe PIDs or other objects, or download all properties at once.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9240 introduces entities grouped into entity domains, names that can be scoped to a particular information resource, and two new resources: a property map fetched with GET and a filtered property map fetched with POST. Address blocks can use hierarchy and inheritance to stay compact.
tldr.outcome: Servers can publish properties for IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, PIDs and later-defined kinds of entity, and clients can download them in bulk or query selected ones. It is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted.

today: RFC 9240 is a Proposed Standard from July 2022. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it, and RFC 9241 builds on it for CDN footprints and capabilities.

sections.title: Three Limits of Endpoint Properties
sections.content:
The base ALTO Protocol (RFC 7285) lets a server attach properties to endpoint addresses through the Endpoint Property Service (EPS). RFC 9240 names three limits of that service.

  • Properties can only belong to individual IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, not to groups of endpoints known as PIDs or to other objects such as Abstract Network Elements.
  • Only globally unique addresses work. A local or anycast address, or a PID name reused in several network maps, is ambiguous.
  • The EPS is POST-only, so a client must name every endpoint it asks about. There is no equivalent of the GET-mode cost map that lets a client download everything once.

The extension answers each limit in turn: a general idea of an entity, names scoped to an information resource, and two new kinds of map resource.
sections.eli5: The old phone book only listed people by street address, only worked for streets with unique names, and made you ask about one house at a time. This update fixes all three problems.

sections.title: Entities, Domains and Property Types
sections.content:
An entity generalizes an ALTO endpoint. It may be an address, but it may also be a PID, an Autonomous System, a country, a network flow, a routing element or an Abstract Network Element. All endpoints are entities, but not all entities are endpoints.

Entities live in an entity domain, a set of entities of the same semantic type. A domain has a type and a name. An entity belongs to exactly one domain, and an identifier points to exactly one entity. Even if a host has both an IPv4 and an IPv6 address, those count as two entities, in the ipv4 and ipv6 domains.

An entity property also has a type and a name, and can carry network-aware or network-agnostic information. Domain types and property types MUST be registered with IANA, except for private-use identifiers starting with priv:. A domain type identifier is at most 64 characters and a property type identifier at most 32.
sections.eli5: An entity is anything on the list, like a kid, a club or a classroom. Each kind lives in its own binder, and every item can have a fact sheet.

sections.title: Naming Domains and Identifying Entities
sections.content:
An entity identifier has the form EntityDomainName ':' DomainTypeSpecificEntityID. The domain name is [ [ ResourceID ] '.' ] EntityDomainType, and the three shapes of that prefix give three categories of domain.

  • Resource-agnostic: just the type, such as ipv4, for entities that mean the same thing everywhere on the server.
  • Resource-specific: a resource ID, a dot, then the type, such as netmap1.pid. This keeps a PID called mypid10 in netmap1 apart from one with the same name in netmap2.
  • Self-defined: a leading dot and the type, for entities that exist only inside the property map that mentions them.

For example, ipv4:192.0.2.14 is an address entity and netmap2.pid:mypid10 is a PID in one particular network map. The dot is not allowed inside a domain type, so there is no ambiguity.

Property names work the same way. A resource-specific property such as netmap1.pid tells which network map the value came from, so one query can ask for the same property type from several resources. The server MUST NOT use a dot inside an information resource identifier.
sections.eli5: If two schools both have a team called the Tigers, you write the school first: Maple.Tigers or Oak.Tigers. Now nobody mixes them up.

sections.title: Hierarchy and Property Inheritance
sections.content:
Some domains have structure. In the ipv4 and ipv6 domains an address block, such as a CIDR prefix, stands for many individual addresses. A server can define a property once on the block instead of listing every address.

The inheritance rule for the Internet address domains is the longest prefix rule. If a property P is not defined for an address but is defined for several blocks containing it, the address inherits P from the block with the longest prefix. Blocks can inherit from larger blocks the same way. This guarantees that an entity never inherits more than one value.

A server MAY say a property has no value by returning JSON null. For an entity that would otherwise inherit a value, null means do not apply inheritance. A server MAY omit entities with no properties, and MAY omit inherited values to save space, so a client MUST NOT assume inherited values are all present. If it needs them, it MUST apply the domain's inheritance rules.

PIDs have no hierarchy or inheritance. PID properties and the properties of the addresses inside that PID are independent, though a server MAY copy some or all PID properties onto its prefixes.
sections.eli5: If the whole street is marked blue, every house on it is blue unless it has its own colour. When two signs cover a house, the most specific one wins.

sections.title: Property Map and Filtered Property Map
sections.content:
The property map is fetched with HTTP GET, uses the media type application/alto-propmap+json and has no input parameters. Its Information Resource Directory (IRD) entry carries a mappings capability that lists each supported entity domain and the property names that can be queried on it. The response holds a property-map object from entity identifiers to property name and value pairs. When the domains depend on other resources, the dependent-vtags field in meta lists their version tags, in the order of the uses field.

The filtered property map is fetched with POST and takes application/alto-propmapparams+json. The request has an entities list and an optional properties list. An empty list means all entities or all properties. If properties is left out, the server returns just the entity identifiers that have at least one property, each with an empty {} value. This is a cheap way to learn which identifiers are valid.

The server MUST answer a missing entities field with E_MISSING_FIELD, and an unknown entity or property with E_INVALID_FIELD_VALUE. A valid entity with no defined properties is not an error. The response MUST include values the requested entities inherit, and the server SHOULD drop identifiers already covered by others in the same response. A client should expect response entities to differ from its request.
sections.eli5: The property map is the full class list with everyone's fact sheet, which you can take in one go. The filtered one is asking the teacher about just a few kids.

sections.title: Domain Types, the pid Property and Legacy Servers
sections.content:
The document defines three initial domain types: ipv4, ipv6 and pid. Individual addresses are aliases of the full-length prefix, so ipv4:192.0.2.0 and ipv4:192.0.2.0/32 are the same entity. The Internet address types are RECOMMENDED for properties tied to addresses, such as an ISP, and the PID type for properties that come from why the PID was formed. For both address and PID domains, the defining information resource MUST be a network map.

It also defines the pid entity property, which keeps the meaning of the RFC 7285 endpoint property and applies to IPv4 and IPv6 entities. Property values may now be any JSON value, where RFC 7285 allowed only strings.

For legacy clients, servers may offer property maps in place of the EPS, but it is recommended that they also provide the EPS for legacy endpoint properties. Entity property maps have no global properties. A property defined by the map itself is a self-defined property, a special case of resource-specific.
sections.eli5: The new system still keeps the old phone book on the desk so people who only know the old way can still look things up.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of the base protocol (Section 15 of RFC 7285) fully apply, including authenticity, confidentiality, privacy and availability. Entity properties may carry more detail than endpoint properties, so requests can reveal a client's activity, and published entities can reveal capabilities, locations or resource availability that others might misuse.

Because a GET-mode property map makes it easy to download many property values, a server should limit it to properties that are not sensitive. Sensitive properties can sit behind a secure URI that needs client authentication, or be offered in coarse form to everyone and finer form to authorized clients. Client and server using the extension are RECOMMENDED to implement incremental updates over server-sent events (RFC 8895) so clients hear of changes promptly, and SHOULD support TLS 1.3.
sections.eli5: If you hand out the whole class list, you must be careful what is written on each fact sheet. Private things should only go to people who are allowed to see them.
